newsitem.title: HONG KONG: First Chinese listing on London market delayed.
newsitem.headline: First Chinese listing on London market delayed.

text.p: Beijing Datang Power Generation Co has delayed its listing plans due to a weak share market, Salomon Brothers, the global coordinator of the share issue, said on Monday of what would have been the first Chinese share listing on the London stock exchange.
"There was a hope to get the transaction done by the new year but the market conditions have not been helpful," said Sarah Hudson, in equity capital markets at Salomon.
She said there was no current timetable for the issue.

Salomon Brothers said in a statement that "despite the recent strength in the equity markets generally, the H-share market continues to be weak as the end of the year approaches", in a reference to Hong-Kong listed Chinese shares.

"As a result, Beijing Datang Power Generation Co Lt and its global coordinator continue to monitor the market to determine the most suitable time for Beijing Datang's initial public offering," the statement said.
Beijing Datang had planned to raise US$300 million through a dual share listing in Hong Kong and London.
The London Financial Times daily reported erlier on Monday that an argument over pricing had delayed the listing.

It said the lead managers, which included Salomon Brothers and British merchant bank Kleinwort Benson, were unable to reach an agreement on a suitable price after a "difficult" meeting in Beijing on Thursday.
The newspaper, quoting unnamed bankers involved in the deal, said Salomon gave the "official" reason as the current weakness of trading in Chinese shares on the Hong Kong market.
